title: Dilations with no Grid
learningGoals: Create a dilation of a figure given a center and scale factor
Explain orally the scale factor's effect on image size and distance from center
Identify center, scale factor and image without a circular grid

correct: C(4,0) twice A-B and D(1,0) half on forward ray
B→C center A factor5, G→E center H factor1/3
F→H center A factor5/4, H→H center B factor1

equivalent: Full measurable straightedge drawing may replace coordinate notation with clear correspondences
A k1 identity map fixes H regardless of selected center
wrong: C placed backward of A for positive factor2
Replace forward G→E factor1/3 with inverse3
Use distance from origin instead of chosen K for perspective
Claim identity k0, which maps point to center, rather than k1
malformed: Perspective drawing without labelled corresponding vertices
Factor unspecified or negative when source only positive
Cool-down only factor number without triangle construction
boundary: Positive k below1 puts image between center and original, k above1 beyond original on ray
If image equals original and point differs from center then k=1
Center itself is fixed by every dilation
Reciprocal factors undo dilations with same center
A dilation k1 is also a rigid motion; k other than1 generally not congruence
A 180-degree line-angle pair contains supplementary78 for vertical102
